pages.text: The stove has no front; what matters is the face your pipe touches.$(br2)$(l)Sides of the bottom layer$()$(li)Pipe $(item)air in$().$(li)Pump $(item)CO2 out$().
$(l)Top and bottom faces$()$(li)Pipe $(item)fuel in$() (creosote or furnace gas).$(li)Pump $(item)hot air out$().$(br2)The $(item)sides of the upper layers$() have no connection at all.

Each input tank takes $(item)only its own fluid$(): air through the bottom sides, fuel through the top or bottom. Anything else is refused, so fuel pushed into a side or hot air flowing back into the top cannot clog the stove. Goggles show what each tank holds.
A simple layout: air and CO2 pipes on two sides of the bottom, a fuel pipe under the stove, and the hot air pump on top, leading to the furnace hatch.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
